facts.claim: Federal rebate for installing an electric heat pump. $2 billion over eight years, aimed at up to 820,000 households.
facts.eligibility: You must live in Canada and own the home (it can be a rental property you own; a home owned by a local Indigenous government counts for residents of that community). One rebate per household, and none if federal money already paid for a heat pump at that address. The heat pump must be on the eligible product list (by AHRI number) and be bought from and installed by an HVAC contractor. Homes heated by electricity (including electric furnaces and baseboards), natural gas, heating oil, propane, diesel, coal or wood can qualify. The higher rebate needs after-tax household income at or below the threshold for your province or territory and household size (see federal-6-income-thresholds).
facts.dates: Online portal opens early 2027 and the program closes in March 2034. Installs from November 1, 2026 can apply once it launches. No payments before launch.
facts.notes: Canada.ca campaign page re-read in full on 2026-11-19 (Government of Canada, National Heat Pump Rebate). It now publishes the income table, eligible homes, fuels and the March 2034 close. It still says program parameters and eligibility criteria are still being finalized and remain subject to change. Earlier source: October 8 news release and PM release. $2 billion for up to 820,000 households.

facts.claim: Portal opens early 2027 and the program closes in March 2034. Households that install an eligible heat pump from November 1, 2026 may apply for a retroactive rebate once the program opens. Receipts must be submitted within 6 months. No payments are made until the program launches and applications are approved.
facts.eligibility: Eligibility is assessed on the program criteria in effect on the date the heat pump was installed. The page says nothing about installs before November 1, 2026. Both emergency and planned installs are accepted; you do not need to remove your old system or show it broke down.
facts.dates: Retroactivity started November 1, 2026. Launch early 2027. Program closes March 2034.
facts.notes: Re-read 2026-11-19 on the Canada.ca campaign page. Parameters are still subject to change, so recheck at the monthly check and when Ottawa publishes the portal date.

facts.claim: Apply in an online portal (early 2027) with no energy audit before or after the install. For the higher rebate you give your Social Insurance Number, which is sent securely to the Canada Revenue Agency to check household income. You buy and install a listed heat pump through an HVAC contractor and submit receipts within 6 months. The October 8 release also said approval within 24 hours and payment approved within five days by direct deposit.
facts.eligibility: Government data cited by CBC: 80 per cent of HVAC replacements happen when the system breaks.
facts.notes: Campaign page re-read 2026-11-19 (SIN and CRA income check, 6-month receipt rule, receipt contents: applicant name and address, installing company, make, model and AHRI number, number of units, total project cost including directly related work such as ductwork and electrical). The 24-hour and five-day timings come from the October 8 release and CBC reading, not the campaign page.

facts.claim: Federal government says the rebates can be combined with existing provincial programs.
facts.eligibility: Each provincial program's own rules on stacking with federal money have not been read against this new program.

facts.claim: Free, direct-install retrofits (insulation, heat pumps) for low-to-median-income homeowners and tenants, delivered through provinces. Moving to Environment and Climate Change Canada. Apply through your province, not the federal government.
facts.eligibility: Provinces accepting applications on the NRCan page: British Columbia, Manitoba, Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island, Quebec.
facts.notes: Page last updated August 31, 2026. Different program from the National Heat Pump Rebate.

facts.program: Federal apartment and rental retrofit programs
facts.claim: CMHC mortgage insurance product supporting up to 250,000 rental units, Canada Infrastructure Bank financing for 30,000 more units, and a Deep Retrofit Accelerator of $110 million over three years starting 2027-28. About 280,000 apartment units to be retrofitted over eight years.
facts.eligibility: For building owners, not individual tenants.

facts.program: National Heat Pump Rebate: income thresholds for the higher rebate
facts.claim: The up-to-$10,000 rebate needs after-tax household income equal to or less than the threshold for your province or territory and household size. Everyone else who qualifies gets $2,000.
facts.amount: up to $10,000 at or below the threshold; $2,000 above it
facts.notes: Read in full on 2026-11-19. Household after-tax income = line 23600 (net income) minus line 43500 (total taxes payable) on the 2025 tax return; add a spouse or common-law partner's. The CRA verifies it through the applicant's SIN when applications open. The table is the published threshold; the program says parameters may still change. Note Saskatchewan 5 or more people (133,034) is lower than 4 people (134,232) as published.

facts.program: National Heat Pump Rebate: who and what qualifies
facts.claim: Homeowners living in Canada can apply, including for a rental property they own. Electricity, natural gas, oil, propane, diesel, coal and wood heat all qualify. The heat pump must be on the eligible product list and installed by an HVAC contractor.
facts.eligibility: One rebate per household even with several properties. No rebate if federal funding was already provided for a heat pump at the address. Rented or leased heat pumps may be eligible once the program launches (details later). The system should heat the whole home and be sized for it. Systems are listed by AHRI number.
facts.notes: Read 2026-11-19. The page cautions that for homes heating with natural gas, switching may not lower bills depending on region and system, and that remote areas may have few certified installers.
